chat: We need somewhere to keep the orders. I say SQLite. It is just one file.
It needs a separate server that we would pay for and look after. We are three students.
I tested SQLite with 200 fake orders and it was fine. What about Firebase?
Okay, SQLite. We expect under 300 orders a day. If it passes 1,000, or a second counter opens, we look again.
The finance office only approves hosted payment pages. We must never store card numbers or UPI PINs.
So we use Razorpay's hosted page. Their test mode worked in two days.
And building our own card form?
Then we would have to protect card data ourselves. No.
Students keep asking at the counter, is my order ready?
Let's send them an SMS when it is ready.
Students asked us not to share their phone numbers with the staff. Staff must never see them on their screen.
Then SMS is awkward. Each alert costs money, about Rs 80 a day, and needs a number.
In-app alerts are free. I tried them with 20 students and they worked.
Done. In-app instead of SMS. We will reconsider if the college pays for an SMS plan.
Last term an outsider ordered food using a student's account.
So only college email addresses can create accounts. Students sign in with the college email and a one-time code.
And no open sign-up with any email. Strangers could place orders on student accounts.
